done_when: forge close accepts a --because file:line that is a line of the base commit when the branch deletes that file, and says in the review block that the evidence is from the base; any other path still needs a line of the reviewed commit; a test covers a deleted file, a present file and a missing line

findings.body: The present-file case only cites a valid reviewed line. It never checks a file shortened by the branch whose cited line still exists in the base. The existing rejection test at tests/test_close.py:375 also lacks that setup. Consequently, an implementation that falls back to any valid base line would pass these tests while violating “any other path still needs a line of the reviewed commit.” Add a case retaining the file, removing a line, and asserting that citing that base-only line is refused.
findings.title: Not done: test rejects base-only lines for files still present

findings.body: For a deleted filename containing non-ASCII characters, such as `café.txt`, Git's default quoting makes the emitted name differ from `path`. The membership check returns false, so a valid base citation is rejected against the reviewed commit. Git documents this behavior for [`--name-only` without `-z`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff). Use NUL-delimited output and split on NUL so deletion detection compares literal filenames.
findings.title: Handle quoted filenames when detecting deletions

why: forge close can't dismiss a finding about a file the branch deletes: --because must cite a line of the reviewed commit, and the deleted file has none (myclaw's migrate PR has a finding about a password in a file the migration deletes)
